## What The Business Is
Microsoft Corp. is a global technology company organized into three reportable segments: **Productivity and Business Processes**, **Intelligent Cloud**, and **More Personal Computing**. Its portfolio spans enterprise software subscriptions, cloud infrastructure, AI services, developer tools, business applications, LinkedIn, Windows, devices, search advertising, and gaming. In FY2025, Microsoft reported $281.7 billion of revenue and $128.5 billion of operating income, with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $168.9 billion. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/investor/reports/ar25/index.html?msockid=3db7fb97e7db61db1f89ed61e6d8602e))

## What It Does
In **Productivity and Business Processes**, Microsoft sells Microsoft 365 Commercial and Consumer, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams, Exchange, SharePoint, Security and Compliance, LinkedIn, and Dynamics 365. In **Intelligent Cloud**, it sells Azure and other cloud services, cloud/AI consumption services, GitHub cloud services, Nuance, virtual desktop, Windows Server, SQL Server, Visual Studio, and enterprise services. In **More Personal Computing**, it sells Windows OEM licensing, Surface/devices, Xbox hardware and content, Game Pass, Bing/Copilot search and news advertising, and Edge-related services. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/investor/reports/ar25/index.html?msockid=09fe5543d85b694b22f743a9d91e684a))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)
Microsoft’s April 29, 2026 FY26 Q3 results were strong: revenue was $82.9 billion, up 18%; operating income was $38.4 billion, up 20%; and diluted EPS was $4.27, up 23% on a GAAP basis. Management said Microsoft Cloud revenue was $54.5 billion, up 29%, and Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 40%, with demand still exceeding available capacity. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2026-q3/press-release-webcast))

AI commercialization accelerated in the transcript period: Microsoft said its AI business surpassed a $37 billion annual revenue run rate, up 123% year over year; Microsoft 365 Copilot paid seats exceeded 20 million; and M365 Commercial Cloud revenue grew 19%. Management also cited over 35,000 paid Fabric customers and broad enterprise agent adoption in the provided call excerpt. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2026-q3/press-release-webcast))

Recent platform news reinforced the AI/cloud strategy. At Build 2026, Microsoft highlighted broader model choice and said Fireworks AI was generally available on Foundry with enterprise governance and Azure data residency; in June, Microsoft also announced a new Pecos, Texas datacenter intended to expand AI-era capacity. ([blogs.microsoft.com](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/06/02/microsoft-build-2026-be-yourself-at-work/))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)
AI growth is coming with margin

## Transcript Read — Long Case

- M365 Copilot paid seats >20M, +250% YoY, fastest growth since launch; Accenture at 740k seats, others >90k.
- Azure revenue growth 40% CC in Q3, Q4 guide 39-40% CC; management expects modest acceleration in second half of CY2026.
- AI business ARR >$37B, +123% YoY.
- Commercial RPO ex-OpenAI +26%, with 12-month revenue recognition up 39%.
- Full-year FY26 operating margins up ~1 pt YoY despite heavy AI investment; FY27 expected double-digit revenue and OI growth.
- Efficiency gains: 40% inference throughput improvement, Maia 200 silicon with 30% better tokens per dollar, faster data center deployment.
- GitHub Copilot transitioning to usage-based pricing; monthly active usage of first-party agents up 6x YTD.
- Security Copilot customers doubled YoY; 35 billion Copilot interactions audited.
- Free cash flow $15.8B, cash from operations $46.7B +26%, supporting investment capacity.

Rationale: Copilot seat acceleration to 20M (250% YoY) and large enterprise wins show AI demand exceeding expectations; Azure growth guidance of 39-40% CC with expected re-acceleration later in the year signals strong cloud momentum; AI ARR surged 123% to $37B; business model shifts to usage-based pricing could drive higher long-term revenue.

## Transcript Read — Short Case

- Calendar 2026 CapEx expected ~$190B, including $25B from higher component pricing; capacity constraints persist through 2026.
- Microsoft Cloud gross margin 66%, down YoY; total company gross margin 68%, down YoY.
- Q4 Windows OEM revenue guide decline in high teens due to laps prior year benefits, inventory normalization, and memory cost-driven PC market softness.

Microsoft's enterprise AI franchise is compounding faster than expected: AI ARR crossed $37B (+123% YoY), Copilot paid seats hit 20M (+250% YoY), and Azure is guided to 39-40% CC growth with expected re-acceleration into 2H CY2026. Commercial RPO ex-OpenAI up 26% signals durable backlog. Management guides FY27 to double-digit revenue AND operating income growth, and FY26 operating margins are up ~1 pt YoY despite the AI capex wave. Efficiency gains (40% inference throughput, Maia 200 silicon +30% tokens/dollar) suggest the ~$190B CY2026 capex is front-loaded for high-return demand, meaning FCF should inflect upward as the capex-to-depreciation cycle matures.

## Bear Case
The ~$190B CY2026 capex figure (including $25B of component-price inflation) is a genuine FCF headwind — TTM FCF of $72.9B is only growing ~5% YoY despite 18% revenue growth, showing capex is currently outrunning cash generation. Microsoft Cloud gross margin fell to 66% and total company GM to 68%, both down YoY. Consumer is weak: Windows OEM guided down high-teens, Xbox content down low-teens, Dynamics bookings softening on model transition. Q4 revenue growth decelerates to 13-15% from 18%. Much of the AI narrative is already priced at a rich ~40x EV/FCF. If AI ROI disappoints or capex fails to translate to FCF, compression is severe.

- **Current implied multiple:** EV $2,913,333M / TTM FCF $72,916M = **~39.9x**
- **12-month forward multiple:** **~36.0x**
- **Direction:** **contract**
- **Top drivers:**
  1. The AI ARR / Copilot catalyst is largely priced at ~40x; incremental beats will be harder to surprise on given elevated expectations.
  2. The $190B capex wave suppresses near-term FCF conversion — while a capex wave can argue for a higher optical multiple, here FCF is still growing (so denominator rises), and margin compression + consumer drag temper enthusiasm, so I favor modest de-rating rather than expansion.

Microsoft’s enterprise AI and cloud cycle remains unusually strong. Azure growth near 40%, AI ARR above $37B and growing 123% YoY, Copilot paid seats above 20M, and commercial RPO strength support durable double-digit revenue and operating income growth into FY27. If capacity additions convert cleanly into Azure AI consumption and Copilot usage pricing scales, forward FCF could exceed my base case despite elevated capex.

## Bear Case
The main risk is that the AI buildout is already heavily priced while free cash flow remains suppressed by the capex wave. CY2026 capex of roughly $190B, lower cloud gross margin, capacity constraints through 2026, and softer Windows/gaming trends could keep FCF conversion weak. If investors question AI ROI or see Azure/Copilot growth decelerate, the current premium FCF multiple could compress more sharply.

## Multiple Re-Rating
Current implied multiple: **39.95x EV/TTM FCF**  
12-month forward multiple: **38.0x EV/FCF**  
Direction: **contract**

Top drivers:
1. **AI upside is real but substantially priced:** Azure 40% growth, AI ARR, and Copilot adoption already support a premium multiple, limiting further expansion.
2. **Capex depresses near-term FCF:** the large AI infrastructure build keeps optical FCF conversion low, which supports a high multiple, but also raises ROI and margin concerns.
3. **Growth remains durable but maturing:** Microsoft should still compound revenue and OI at double-digit rates, but the market is likely to demand evidence that AI capex converts into sustained FCF before expanding the multiple.

**2,913,332.6 - 2,888,472.6 = $24,860.0M**
